**F-2 (`_difficulty.md` § findings) — consequence on task 1.**

`days_to_decision = DAYS('2026-08-15', '2026-08-22') = 7 ≤ K('prompt_report_days') = 8`, and
`declined_reviews = COUNT(drive_damage_reviews, review_status='declined') = 1`
(`1bbc723f-…`, the fuel dispute, `decided_at: "2026-08-19 13:15:00 PDT"`). So the extended policy's
**second** `admin_element` tier fires: `P('damage_admin_fee_usd') × K('reopened_admin_multiple')
= 95.00 × 1.5 = 142.50`.

Base `drive_damage_and_recharges` says of the same charge: *"The class's damage administration charge is
added once per incident and never once per damaged part."* Honouring that inherited sentence gives
`admin_element = 95.00`.

Recomputed on this world, everything else unchanged:

| reading | `admin_element` | scored recharge | scored dispute that follows |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| extended as written | `142.50` | **`903.00`** | **`464.05`** |
| base sentence honoured | `95.00` | **`855.50`** | `disputable_base = 855.50 − 95.00 = 760.50`; `insured_part = 456.30`; `after_insurance = 304.20`; `× 100 %` `+ 125.00 + 15.85` = **`445.05`** |

Two defensible figures for **both** scored parameters of this task, and
`drive_ext_damage_recharge.overwrite` is `[]`, so nothing tells a reader which clause yields. The
deviation is carried entirely by a multiplier on a base quantity, with no new parameter name on the
money — the "anonymous intermediate factor" pattern. `SOURCE-POLICY RED`.

**F-6 (`_difficulty.md` § findings) — checked and does not bite here.** Base recharges damage *"up to the
rate class's waiver excess **where the waiver was carried**, and in full where it was not."* This rental
**did** carry the waiver: `drive_rental_entries` holds a `collision_damage_waiver` line of `129.95` on
`c390c49a-…`. The live limb is therefore "up to the waiver excess" = `950.00`, and the extended figure's
damage component before the administration charge is `760.50 ≤ 950.00`. No conflict in this world.

**O-2 (`_difficulty.md`) — checked and does not bite here.** The extended rule says *"the renter's own
record of rental damage claims in the last twenty-four months"* without saying where they were filed;
the `compute` reads `care` claims while this charter also publishes `drive_msr_damage_claims_24m`
("count of `drive_damage_charge` rows … in the last 24 months"). Both readings return **1** on this
world — the `care` reading counts `care_claims/fd5eec81-…` (`claim_type: "rental_damage"`,
`filed_date: "2025-09-14"`, 11 months back); the drive reading counts the `damage_charge` of `480.00` on
rental `95f1f2c4-…` (`posted_date: "2025-09-12"`, also inside 24 months). Same count, same tier
(`single_claim_loading_pct`), same number. No second figure.

**O-3 (`_difficulty.md`) — confirmed on this world.** `administration_element`'s first tier ("days to
decision beyond the damage reporting window") cannot be reached here: `days_to_decision = 7` and the
window is `10`, and had the decision fallen outside the window the base `inside_damage_window` gate would
already have forbidden the recharge. The tier costs this task no number.

**F-4** does not bear on this task: `goodwill_put_back` belongs to `drive_ext_cancellation_refund`, which
this task's tree does not contain.

### problem_chain

Walked out from the root problem using the policy and the world alone.

**Root problem.** What the customer brings is: *"he wants the thing formally challenged, in his name, so
that it is on record and somebody has to look at it properly before anyone takes money off him"*, and
*"he is not asking for a refund, he is not asking anybody to lean on the supplier"*. That is a recharge
put in dispute in the renter's own name — `drive_ext_recharge_dispute` (`computes: disputed_amount_usd`,
`target_tool: raise_recharge_dispute_65c619e1`, `owner="user"`). No other extended policy registers a
challenge.

**Its prerequisite sentences.** `drive_ext_recharge_dispute.rule` opens with exactly one sentence joining
its own result to something it waits on:

> *"The amount a renter may put in dispute is fixed only once the ledger carries the entry for the damage
> the rental desk has approved against the rental."*

**Does that state hold at `frozen_time`?** No. Scanning `initial_state.drive_rental_entries` for
`drive_rental_id = "c390c49a-49ea-4764-8f9c-9d8d3ac9cc97"` — fourteen rows: one `agency_service_fee`
(`9.95`), five `rental_rate` (`54.00` each), a `mileage_grant` (`+1000` miles), a `mileage_use`
(`−860`), `collision_damage_waiver` (`129.95`), `theft_protection` (`59.95`), `vehicle_licence_fee`
(`21.25`), `sales_tax` (`23.63`), `fuel_refuelling_service` (`63.39`) and `cleaning_fee` (`125.00`).
**No `damage_charge` line.** `recharge_on_ledger = SUM(… charge_category='damage_charge')` over this
rental = **`0.00`**. The prerequisite is genuinely unmet at the opening.

*Near-miss on this very edge.* `drive_rental_entries` **does** carry a `damage_charge` of `480.00` in the
renter's own name — on his **other** rental `95f1f2c4-…` (`RA4417003`, Seattle, `closed`,
`posted_date: "2025-09-12"`). A reader who sums the customer's damage recharges rather than the
rental's finds `480.00` and concludes the prerequisite is already met. Excluded by the rule's
"against the rental" and by the DSL's scoping of `SUM` to the target holding.

*A second thing that is present but is not the state.* `drive_damage_reviews/5e463211-…` stands
**approved** against this rental. A reader might take "the damage the rental desk has approved" to be
satisfied by the approved review itself. The sentence is explicit that what is waited on is *"the
**ledger** carries the entry for"* that damage — an entry on `drive_rental_entries`, not a review. The
approved review is the base *eligibility* for making the entry, and it is exactly what makes the
prerequisite problem resolvable now rather than a wait.

**Which write brings that state about?** `drive_ext_damage_recharge.rule` opens *"The amount recharged to
a renter for damage the rental desk has approved against the rental is built from …"* — the only policy
of this charter whose result is an amount recharged for approved damage. Its `target_tool` is
`post_damage_recharge_2d59c35f`, `owner="agent"`. One reading only.

**Does that problem have prerequisites of its own?** `drive_ext_damage_recharge.prerequisite: []`, and
its `rule` carries no sentence joining its result to a waited-on state or action with an ordering
connective. Its inputs are all seeded. The walk terminates.

**The tree the auditor derived:**

```
drive_ext_recharge_dispute      (root, USER, raise_recharge_dispute_65c619e1)
        │  value_input  — gate: recharge_on_ledger
        ▼
drive_ext_damage_recharge       (leaf, agent, post_damage_recharge_2d59c35f)
```

- nodes: 2 — one root problem, **one** prerequisite problem (n = 1, within the 1–3 band)
- edges: 1, `kind: value_input`. Floor `max(n−1, 1) = 1` → **met**.
- cycles: none.
- topological order: `drive_ext_damage_recharge` → `drive_ext_recharge_dispute`.

**Per-edge load-bearing run.** Skip the prerequisite write, replay everything else unchanged:
`recharge_on_ledger` stays `0.00` → `disputable_base = MX(0.00 − 95.00, 0.0) = 0.00` (the declined-review
tier still applies) → `insured_part = 0.00` → `after_insurance = 0.00` → `after_share = 0.00` → result =
`RND(MX(0.00 + 125.00 + 15.8475, 0.0), 2)` = **`140.85`**, against `464.05` with the write in place. A
swing of `323.20`. **The edge bears weight.**

**Parallel edges.** None — a single edge, so no shared balance, cap or dedup key admits two orders.

**No-wait argument.** The resolving action is one `ctx.create` by the agent, on an assessment already
decided four days before `frozen_time`, inside a reporting window that closes the day after
`frozen_time`. Nothing external intervenes.

**The tool layer judges no prerequisite.** `post_damage_recharge_2d59c35f` (task_tools.py:116–166) is
`make_id` → `round` → one `ctx.create("drive_rental_entries", …)` → return; `raise_recharge_dispute_65c619e1`
(task_tools.py:169–221) is `make_id` → `round` → one `ctx.create("drive_damage_reviews", …)` → return.
Neither has a conditional, a raise, or a read of another row; neither refuses, errors or hints while the
prerequisite is unresolved.

**A customer's own write is in the tree.** The **root** is `raise_recharge_dispute_65c619e1`, carrying
`@tool(owner="user", rw="write")`, and the persona executes it passively at the agent's hand-over:
*"When the agent hands the challenge over for him to put through in his own name, he does it there and
then and reads back what comes up."* ✓

**The customer raises only the root problem.** *"He does not know how the desk works out what he is being
held responsible for, and he never asks for the figure in advance."* He never names the recharge as
something that must happen first; the prerequisite reaches him only if the **agent** explains it, and
even then he only assents: *"If the agent explains that the assessment has been approved on the
supplier's side, that the charge therefore has to go on the rental before anything can be challenged …
he says that is not what he would have chosen but he understands it and to carry on."* That is a passive
if/else reaction to the agent's own explanation, not the customer supplying the tree.

The declined fuel dispute — a factor input, not a prerequisite — is likewise gated behind the agent
asking: *"He also mentions, **only if the agent raises** the state of the account or asks whether anything
else is in dispute, that he already had a row with them about a refuelling charge on the same rental and
was told no; he will not say what he thinks that means for this."* And it is on the record anyway
(`drive_damage_reviews/1bbc723f-…`), so it is corroboration rather than a hidden input.

**No second item of work, and the persona closes where the work closes.** He asks for nothing besides the
challenge — no refund ("he is not asking for a refund"), no pressure on the supplier, no document to send.
*"If, at the end, he is told the challenge is open with the rental desk, he asks how long these usually
take, thanks them for doing it properly, and rings off."* ✓

### task_independent_derivation

**Need, authorisation, timing.** He wants the damage recharge on rental `RA5028741` formally challenged
**in his own name**, **now** ("so that it is on record and somebody has to look at it properly before
anyone takes money off him"). The authorisation split is stated, not inferred: the challenge is his own
act, which he performs when handed over; the desk's own side he leaves to the desk ("Anything about what
the supplier's inspector actually saw, how the body shop priced it, or where the insurer stands, he says
straight out that he cannot answer and leaves with the desk"). He is explicit he will not simply pay
("he is not going to pay it quietly and argue later").

**Act now / wait / refuse: ACT NOW**, both steps. All three base gates on the recharge hold (table above);
the dispute is a review registration that base expressly contemplates. Nothing defers either write, and
nothing refuses them — this is not one of the uncovered grounds in `blueprint.yaml`'s summary (it is not a
personal injury claim, not a dispute with a road authority, not a counter upsell, not a replacement
vehicle demand, and the rental was booked through the agency).

**Object.** The narrowest business object is rental `c390c49a-49ea-4764-8f9c-9d8d3ac9cc97`
(`RA5028741`, `HRTZ`, intermediate, `PDXD1`, `2026-08-10` → `2026-08-15`, `Pay At Counter Flex Rate`),
correlated by `drive_rental_id`. The other rental `95f1f2c4-…` is excluded: `closed`, 2025, Seattle,
different supplier — and it is the carrier of the `480.00` near-miss. The review both writes quote is
`5e463211-184d-4e86-8bd8-3f5ccdd839be`, the **approved** `damage_assessment`; the declined
`1bbc723f-…` is a `fuel_dispute` and is evidence for two factor tiers, not the incident under dispute.

**Verbatim arguments.** `post_damage_recharge_2d59c35f.damage_reference` is Verbatim class, "the
supplier's own reference for the damaged vehicle **as it is recorded on that rental damage review**" →
`"HRTZ-DMG-55217"` from `drive_damage_reviews/5e463211-….evidence_reference`.
`raise_recharge_dispute_65c619e1.evidence_reference` is Verbatim class, "taken from **what the renter
reads out in this conversation**" → `"PDX-RET-40912"`, which the persona reads out: *"he reads out the
return inspection slip number, PDX-RET-40912"*. The two are different references from different sources,
and each tool's docstring names its own source unambiguously.

**Reachability.** `find_customers(full_name="Tomas Ferreira")` → the profile; `verify_traveller_identity`
with two of {mobile 7040562137, DOB 1982-11-02, passport_last4 4318} — all three are offered in order,
with postcode 97209 in reserve. `find_drive_rentals(customer_id=…)` → both rentals;
`find_drive_rental_entries(drive_rental_id=…)` → the fourteen rows; `find_drive_damage_reviews(drive_rental_id=…)`
→ both reviews; `find_club_memberships(customer_id=…)` → Silver/active; `find_care_policies(customer_id=…)`
→ TripGuard Plus (in force) and the expired Trip Basics Standard; `find_care_claims(customer_id=…)` →
the 2025 rental-damage claim. Every policy input is reachable; nothing is hidden in the seed only.

**Near-miss records present in this world.**

- *Computation A:* `drive_rental_entries` — the `damage_charge` of `480.00` on the **other** rental
  `95f1f2c4-…`; a reader who counts the customer's damage recharges rather than the rental's both thinks
  the prerequisite already met and mis-sizes the basis. Also `care_policies/3628ffb0-…`
  (`Trip Basics Standard`, **`expired`**, `rental_damage_limit_usd: 0.0`) — a real travel protection
  policy in the renter's name that `EXISTS('care', status='in_force')` correctly ignores; a reader who
  takes "holds a travel protection policy" without the status filter finds the wrong policy. And the
  `care` claim sits on **that expired policy**, so "the claim and the in-force policy are the same
  contract" is a natural and wrong inference — the rule keeps the two conditions separate and this world
  makes them come apart.
- *Computation B:* `drive_damage_reviews/1bbc723f-…` — a **declined** review on this rental that is a
  `fuel_dispute`, not a damage assessment. `challenge_scope` and `administration_element` read it
  through `review_status='declined'` alone (so it counts), while `fuel_challenged` reads it through
  `review_type='fuel_dispute'` **and** `review_status='declined'` (so it counts there too), and
  `assessment_decided_on` reads `review_status='approved'` (so it does **not**). A reader who lets the
  declined fuel dispute stand in for the decided assessment gets `window_days_used` and
  `days_to_decision` wrong. The persona plants it deliberately: *"he already had a row with them about a
  refuelling charge on the same rental and was told no."*

**No stamp names the outcome.** No field of `drive_rentals`, `drive_rental_entries`,
`drive_damage_reviews`, `club_memberships`, `care_policies` or `care_claims` in this world carries a
share, loading, uplift, relief or band label. Every tier is reached from a ledger aggregate, a date span
or a cross-category parameter. `drive_damage_reviews.disputed_amount_usd` on the approved review is
`0.00`, so it does not pre-announce the recharge either.

**Cross-difficulty evidence is seeded and consistent.** `care` is a genuine sibling difficulty
(`travel_protection_desk`, categories `[care]`). Two `care_policies` rows and one `care_claims` row stand
in `initial_state` for this customer. `TripGuard Plus` carries `rental_damage_limit_usd: 25000.0` and
`rental_damage_deductible_usd: 250.0` in `products/care.yaml`, and `Trip Basics Standard` carries `0.0`
for both — both seeded rows match their charter, and the claim's `claim_type: "rental_damage"` is a value
`db_schema.json:care_claims.claim_type` actually permits. `club_memberships/021b108f-…` is likewise
seeded and matches `products/club.yaml` (`Wanderlane Silver` ⇒ `car_rental_discount_pct: 3`).

**Counts against the bounds.** Computation A: 6 factors (5 `parameter`, 1 `method`) ✓. Computation B:
5 factors (4 `parameter`, 1 `method`) ✓. Over the task: **5 multi-source** factors
(`excess_borne_relief`, `protection_deduction`, `claim_record_loading`, `cleaning_challenged`,
`fuel_challenged`) ≥ 1 ✓; **3 `cross_difficulty`** factors (`excess_borne_relief` → club,
`claim_record_loading` → care, `protection_answered` → care) ≥ 1 ✓, of which two read a genuine sibling
difficulty. All eleven factors survive the weight tests.

## findings

---

**Finding 1-1 — `SOURCE-POLICY RED` (charter-global F-2; consequence demonstrated here).**

- **Verdict.** RED.
- **Symptom.** On this world **both** scored parameters have two defensible values —
  `903.00` / `464.05` under the extended rule, `855.50` / `445.05` if the inherited base sentence about
  the damage administration charge is honoured.
- **Root cause.** `drive_ext_damage_recharge` overrides a base sentence of `drive_damage_and_recharges`
  without declaring it: `overwrite: []`. The deviation is carried by a bare multiplier on a base
  quantity (`reopened_admin_multiple: 1.5`), which is why it escapes a name-level check — the classic
  "anonymous intermediate factor".
- **Evidence.** base `drive_damage_and_recharges.rule`: *"The class's damage administration charge is
  added **once per incident** and never once per damaged part."* — extended
  `drive_ext_damage_recharge.rule`: *"… where the damage was decided within the prompt report days and a
  review already stands declined against the rental the administration charge is added at the **reopened
  administration multiple**."* — `compute.admin_element` — world:
  `drive_rentals/c390c49a-….returned_at = "2026-08-15 08:45:00 PDT"`,
  `drive_damage_reviews/5e463211-….decided_at = "2026-08-22 16:40:00 PDT"` (7 days, ≤ 8),
  `drive_damage_reviews/1bbc723f-….review_status = "declined"` (count 1),
  `Pay At Counter Flex Rate.damage_admin_fee_usd = 95.0`.
- **Demonstrated consequence.** Recomputed on this world:
  `admin_element = 142.50` → recharge `RND(760.4982 + 142.50, 2) = 903.00`, and the dispute that reads it
  gives `disputable_base = 808.00` → `464.05`.
  `admin_element = 95.00` → recharge `RND(760.4982 + 95.00, 2) = 855.50`, and the dispute gives
  `disputable_base = 760.50`, `insured_part = 456.30`, `after_insurance = 304.20`, `× 100 %`, `+ 125.00`,
  `+ 15.85` = `445.05`. The defect propagates across the prerequisite edge into the root problem's score.
- **Affected artifact and location.** `env/online_travel_agency/tasks/car_rental_desk/drive.extended.yaml`
  — `extended_policies[2] drive_ext_damage_recharge.overwrite` (empty), `.rule` (the administration
  sentences), `.compute.admin_element`, `.params.reopened_admin_multiple`,
  `.factors[administration_element]`; and `policies[drive_damage_and_recharges].rule`. Scored solution
  affected: `evaluation_criteria[9]`'s `damage_recharge_usd` **and** `evaluation_criteria[11]`'s
  `disputed_amount_usd`.
- **Relation to previous revisions.** First revision; no prior audit exists for this difficulty.

---

**Finding 1-2 — observation. The persona's "ten days later" cannot be true at `frozen_time`.**

`user_scenario` says he *"dropped it back at the downtown branch on the Saturday morning"* — matching
`returned_at: "2026-08-15 08:45:00 PDT"`, a Saturday — and then *"**Ten days later** the rental company
wrote to say they were holding him responsible for damage to the offside rear."* Ten days after
2026-08-15 is 2026-08-25, which is **after** `frozen_time: "2026-08-24 14:30:00 PDT"`. The letter cannot
have arrived. The authoritative record is `drive_damage_reviews/5e463211-….decided_at = "2026-08-22"`,
seven days after the return, and every scored input reads that record rather than the persona, so **no
scored value moves** and this is not a red light. It is nonetheless a persona-to-world inconsistency on a
date that sits next to two scored ladders (`report_promptness` turns on 7 vs 8 days; `assessment_timing_share`
turns on `7 × 3 > 10 × 2`), and an agent that took the caller's "ten days" as the decision date would
land on `report_share_pct = 75` and `admin_element = 95.00` — a wrong answer reached by believing the
customer. Recorded as an observation because the policy tells the agent to read the record.

---

**Finding 1-3 — observation (charter-global F-6, checked on this world and inert).** Base recharges damage
*"up to the rate class's waiver excess where the waiver was carried, and **in full where it was not**"*,
but `drive_ext_damage_recharge` has no "in full" branch and no input for the actual cost of the damage —
`excess_borne` always starts from `P('cdw_excess_usd')`. This rental carried the waiver (a
`collision_damage_waiver` line of `129.95` stands on it), so the live limb is "up to the waiver excess"
and the extended damage component (`760.50`) sits under `950.00`. No second number here; the gap would
open on a world with no waiver sold, which this difficulty does not present.

---

**Finding 1-4 — observation (charter-global O-2, checked on this world and inert).** The extended rule
says *"the renter's own record of rental damage claims in the last twenty-four months"* without saying
where they were filed; the `compute` reads `care` claims, while this same charter publishes
`drive_msr_damage_claims_24m` over `drive_damage_charge` rows. On this world both readings return **1**
— the `care` claim `fd5eec81-…` filed `2025-09-14` (11 months back) and the drive recharge of `480.00`
posted `2025-09-12` on the other rental — so both select `single_claim_loading_pct` and the number is
identical. The ambiguity is real in the wording and costs this task nothing.

---

**Finding 1-5 — observation (charter-global O-3, confirmed on this world).**
`administration_element`'s first tier ("days to decision beyond the reporting window") is unreachable
whenever base's `inside_damage_window` gate holds, because the decision necessarily precedes
`frozen_time`. Here `days_to_decision = 7` against a window of `10`. The ladder therefore has three
stated tiers but only two that any admissible world can take. No consequence on this task's score.

---

**Finding 1-6 — observation. The dispute policy's `subject` does not name the record its tool writes.**
`drive_ext_recharge_dispute.subject: [drive_damage_charge]`, but `raise_recharge_dispute_65c619e1` writes
a `drive_damage_reviews` row and posts no ledger line — and `blueprint.yaml`'s claimed `event_types` for
this difficulty carry no review-creation event the subject could have named instead. Structural only; no
scored value and no eligibility turns on it. (Recorded charter-globally as `_difficulty.md` O-6.)

---

**Finding 1-7 — no finding on the derivation.** The auditor's independent derivation reproduced GT
exactly: both scored parameters, both tool identities, both owners, the order, all ten write arguments
including both Verbatim-class references, the terminal ledger and review, the whole problem tree, both
whole-baseline figures and all eleven factor-sensitivity figures — every one derived from the policy, the
world and the tool contracts alone, before the reveal. No arithmetic, wording or structural discrepancy
was found between the frozen derivation and GT.

---

`admin_element = 95.00` → recharge `855.50`, dispute `445.05` — is **no longer defensible**, because the
base sentence that grounded it is declared superseded by name. The propagation across the prerequisite
edge that made this the more serious of the two round-1 reds is closed with it.

**1-5 / O-3 — CLOSED, and genuinely reachable.** The retired tier was *"the days to decision are beyond
the rate class's damage reporting window → nothing"*, which base's `inside_damage_window` gate made
unreachable: the recharge is forbidden once `frozen_time` is past `returned_at + damage_report_window_days`,
and the decision necessarily precedes `frozen_time`. The replacement is *"Where more than one damage
assessment stands approved against the rental the administration charge is added once for each approved
assessment"*, implemented as `P('damage_admin_fee_usd') * approved_assessments if approved_assessments > 1`.

Tested, not assumed:
- *Reachable?* Yes. It needs two approved `damage_assessment` reviews on one rental. Base's
  `damage_assessment_approved` gate requires **at least** one, `drive_damage_reviews` carries no
  per-rental uniqueness constraint in `db_schema.json`, and this very rental already carries two reviews
  (one approved, one declined) — so a second approved row is an ordinary world, not an excluded one.
  Contrast the retired tier, which no admissible world could reach.
- *Base-consonant?* Yes, and independently of the declaration: base fixes the charge at once *per
  incident* and forbids once *per damaged part*. One charge per approved assessment is one per incident,
  and the "never per damaged part" limb is untouched. The rework did not merely reword an unreachable
  tier into a reachable one — it chose a rung that base's own principle supplies.
- *Does it disturb this world?* No: `approved_assessments = 1`, so the tier does not fire and `142.50`
  stands.

**1-2 — CLOSED.** Revision 1 recorded that the persona's *"Ten days later the rental company wrote"* put
the letter at `2026-08-25`, after `frozen_time 2026-08-24 14:30:00 PDT` — it could not have arrived. The
line now reads *"**The Saturday after that** the rental company wrote to say they were holding him
responsible."* He dropped the vehicle back on Saturday `2026-08-15`; the Saturday after that is
`2026-08-22`, which is **before** `frozen_time` and is exactly
`drive_damage_reviews/5e463211-….decided_at = "2026-08-22 16:40:00 PDT"`. Persona and record now agree on
the date, and the caller's own account no longer points an agent at a wrong `days_to_decision`. The two
ladders that turn on it — `report_promptness` (7 vs 8 days) and `assessment_timing_share`
(`7 × 3 > 10 × 2`) — are unaffected, and both keep their revision-1 tiers.

**1-3 / F-6 — CLOSED.** Base's *"Damage discovered at return or afterwards is recharged … up to the rate
class's waiver excess where the waiver was carried, and in full where it was not."* is now named in
`overwrite`, replaced by *"The excess the renter bears is the rate class's waiver excess."* The limb the
extended policy had no input for is retired explicitly rather than ignored. On this world nothing moves —
the rental carried the waiver (`collision_damage_waiver` line of `129.95`), so the live limb was always
the one the extended implements.

**1-4 / O-2 — CLOSED.** The rule now says *"the renter's own record of rental damage claims **filed on
their travel protection policies**"* in its opening sentence and in both ladder tiers, and the baseline
sentence carries the same wording. The ambiguity revision 1 recorded — `care_claims` or this charter's own
`drive_msr_damage_claims_24m` — is resolved inside the rule rather than in a note a document reader may
never see. The value was and remains `10 %` either way on this world.

**1-6 / O-6 — unchanged, argued.** `drive_ext_recharge_dispute.subject` is still `[drive_damage_charge]`
while `raise_recharge_dispute_65c619e1` writes `drive_damage_reviews`. Re-verified: the fact stands, and
so does the reason it is only an observation — `blueprint.yaml`'s claimed `event_types` for this
difficulty contain no review-creation event the subject could name instead, so there is no correct
alternative value, and no scored value or eligibility turns on it.
